referents.why: 'your proud waves': the second person of the LORD's speech is the sea, which is not among the candidates.
'I declared': the first person, the LORD. The builder's self-reference is replaced.
referents.category: implied first person in the speech

referents.why: 'you may come this far': the addressee of this speech is the sea, not a candidate.
'but no farther': the same addressee, the sea, not a candidate.
'here someone will set your waves': a third masc sing with no masculine singular candidate that is a sensible doer; the waves are plural, and the form is impersonal.

links.why: 'I declared: you may come this far ...' The saying clause has its said clause as content (R1); the turn holds the parts.
Wrong direction and wrong relation. The speech is inside the saying, not after it.
'you may come this far, and not add': a plain and between two clauses.
'but no farther; here ...': the waw joins the next clause; not a result or purpose.

groups.why: The sender was a slot id; the LORD declares. The addressee (the sea) is not a candidate and is left open, recorded in cant_tell.

cant_tell.what: The addressee of the speech, the sea to which 'you' refers
cant_tell.why: The sea is not among the candidates, so the turn's addressee cannot be filled.

cant_tell.what: Whether this speech is nested in the LORD's speech turn Job.38.1#g1
cant_tell.why: The nesting is not linked from this verse.

cant_tell.what: The subject of 'here someone will set'
cant_tell.why: The third masc sing is impersonal, and no masc sing candidate is a sensible doer.
